question: What is scored as a 'pull-up' during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_b: Stopping without changing direction
choice_c: Any use of the horn during the exercise
choice_d: Checking a mirror before backing
explanation: A pull-up is pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: Are applicants penalized for initial pull-ups during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: No, but an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors
choice_b: Yes, every single pull-up is an automatic failure
choice_c: Pull-ups are never counted in scoring
choice_d: Only the first pull-up is penalized
explanation: Applicants will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What is an 'encroachment' during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors or unique parts at or higher than door mirror height
choice_b: Sounding the horn at the wrong time
choice_c: Failing to signal before a turn
choice_d: Exceeding the posted speed limit during the exercise
explanation: An encroachment is touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle, other than the vehicle's mirrors (door or fender) or other unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What is scored as a 'look' during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Opening the door or moving from a seated position (or on a bus, walking to the back to get a better view) while in physical control of the vehicle
choice_b: Glancing at the mirrors while driving forward
choice_c: Checking traffic before a turn
choice_d: Reading the exercise instructions
explanation: If at any time the applicant opens the door, moves from a seated position while in physical control of the vehicle, or (on a bus) walks to the back to get a better view, it is scored as a look.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: How many free looks are allowed on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) versus Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: One free look on Exercise 2, two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_b: Two free looks on Exercise 2, one free look on Exercise 4
choice_c: Unlimited free looks on both exercises
choice_d: No free looks are allowed on either exercise
explanation: Applicants may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 (Straight-line Backing) and two free looks on Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing) to check the position of the vehicle.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What must an applicant do upon completion of each Basic Control Skills exercise to signal completion?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn
choice_b: Turn off the engine completely
choice_c: Exit the vehicle and inform the examiner verbally
choice_d: Flash the headlights twice
explanation: Upon completion of an exercise, the applicant must set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn to indicate the exercise is complete.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What are the four Basic Control Skills test exercises, in order?
choice_a: Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, and Reverse Offset Backing
choice_b: Parallel Parking, Alley Dock, Straight Backing, and Three-Point Turn
choice_c: Forward Stop, Reverse Offset Backing, Straight-Line Backing, and Forward Offset Tracking
choice_d: Only two exercises: Forward Stop and Reverse Backing
explanation: The Basic Control Skills test includes Step 1 - Forward Stop, Step 2 - Straight-Line Backing, Step 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and Step 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12, Basic Control Skills Test

question: During Exercise 1 (Forward Stop), how many times may the applicant stop?
choice_a: Only once
choice_b: Up to three times
choice_c: As many times as needed to align correctly
choice_d: Stopping is not required for this exercise
explanation: During Exercise 1, the applicant drives forward through the alley and stops with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley, and may stop only once.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.2.1, Exercise 1, Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2 (Straight Line Backing), how many free pull-ups are allowed, and how many times may the applicant safely exit the vehicle to check around it?
choice_a: One free pull-up, and one exit to check around the vehicle
choice_b: Two free pull-ups, and two exits
choice_c: Unlimited pull-ups, but no exits allowed
choice_d: No pull-ups or exits are allowed
explanation: In Exercise 2, the applicant is allowed one free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around the vehicle.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.2.2, Exercise 2, Straight Line Backing

question: During Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking), is the applicant allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle?
choice_a: No, the applicant is not allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle during this exercise
choice_b: Yes, stopping is required at the midpoint
choice_c: Backing up is allowed if the applicant misjudges the turn
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle is allowed once to check clearance
explanation: During Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking), the applicant is NOT allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle; if the applicant stops, the exercise will be ended.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing), how close to the rear of the alley must the rear most part of the vehicle come to stop?
choice_a: Within three feet of the rear of the alley
choice_b: Within one foot of the rear of the alley
choice_c: Exactly touching the rear boundary
choice_d: Within ten feet of the rear of the alley
explanation: In Exercise 4, the applicant offset backs into the alley, bringing the rear most part of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley, stopping in the three-foot box at the end.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: In Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing), how many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups, and up to two exits to check around the vehicle
choice_b: One free pull-up, and one exit
choice_c: No pull-ups or exits are allowed
choice_d: Unlimited pull-ups and exits
explanation: In Exercise 4, the applicant is allowed two free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around the vehicle.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: Must the Basic Control Skills test be passed before an applicant can proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: Yes, the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before proceeding to the Road Test
choice_b: No, the two tests can be taken in either order
choice_c: Only the Road Test needs to be passed; Basic Control is optional
choice_d: They are combined into a single simultaneous test
explanation: The manual reminds applicants that the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before they can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 12) -- Section 12.2.4, Road Test

question: What three things must a driver do at all times during the On-Road Driving test?
choice_a: Wear the safety belt, obey all traffic signs/signals/laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation
choice_b: Maintain exactly the speed limit at all times, use only the right lane, and avoid all turns
choice_c: Keep the radio off, avoid using turn signals, and drive below the speed limit
choice_d: Only obey traffic signals; other rules are relaxed for testing
explanation: During the On-Road Driving test, the driver must wear their safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: If the test route does not have a certain traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing, what may the examiner ask the applicant to do?
choice_a: Simulate the traffic situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing
choice_b: Skip that portion of the test entirely with no substitute
choice_c: Automatically fail that section
choice_d: Drive to another city to find the missing traffic feature
explanation: If the test route does not have certain traffic situations, the applicant may be asked to simulate the traffic situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing if they were in that situation.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: What defines 'unsafe coasting' during a turn on the On-Road Driving test?
choice_a: The vehicle being out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
choice_b: Coasting for any distance whatsoever
choice_c: Coasting only while going downhill
choice_d: Coasting is never considered unsafe during a turn
explanation: Unsafe coasting occurs when the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle before a turn, where should a driver stop?
choice_a: Where they can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of them (a safe gap)
choice_b: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead to save space
choice_c: At least one full car length beyond the vehicle ahead
choice_d: Position does not matter as long as the vehicle is stopped
explanation: If stopping behind another vehicle, the driver should stop where they can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of them, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: When driving through an intersection during the test, is a driver permitted to change lanes while proceeding through it?
choice_a: No, the driver should not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_b: Yes, lane changes are encouraged to demonstrate skill
choice_c: Only if a turn signal is used
choice_d: Lane changes are required at every intersection
explanation: When driving through an intersection, the driver should not change lanes while proceeding through it, decelerating and yielding to pedestrians and traffic as needed.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the test, in which lane should the vehicle generally be centered?
choice_a: The right-most lane
choice_b: The center lane, regardless of number of lanes
choice_c: The left-most lane
choice_d: Whichever lane has the least traffic
explanation: During the urban business portion of the test, the vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.3, Urban Business

question: Once exiting the expressway onto the exit ramp, what must a driver continue to do?
choice_a: Continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between vehicles
choice_b: Accelerate to merge back into expressway traffic
choice_c: Stop immediately at the top of the ramp
choice_d: Turn off the headlights
explanation: Once on the exit ramp, the driver must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between their vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.5, Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: During the Stop/Start maneuver, once the vehicle is stopped, what must the driver activate before setting the parking brake?
choice_a: The four-way emergency flashers
choice_b: The high beam headlights
choice_c: The horn, repeatedly
choice_d: Nothing needs to be activated once stopped
explanation: Once stopped during the Stop/Start maneuver, the driver must cancel the turn signal, activate the four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and move the gear shift to neutral or park.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume from the Stop/Start maneuver, in what order should the driver turn off the flashers and activate a turn signal?
choice_a: Turn off the four-way flashers, then activate the left turn signal
choice_b: Activate the left turn signal first, then turn off the flashers
choice_c: Both should be done simultaneously with no set order
choice_d: Only the flashers need to be addressed; a turn signal is not required
explanation: When instructed to resume, the driver should check traffic and mirrors, turn off the four-way flashers, activate the left turn signal, then release the parking brake and pull straight ahead when traffic permits.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

topic: Railroad Crossings During the Road Test
question: While any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing, what actions must a driver avoid?
choice_a: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
choice_b: Only changing lanes; other actions are fine
choice_c: Only using the horn
choice_d: There are no restricted actions while crossing tracks
explanation: While any part of the vehicle is in the crossing, a driver must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

topic: Railroad Crossings During the Road Test
question: If driving a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle, within what distance from the nearest rail must the vehicle stop at a railroad crossing during the test?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: Exactly at the cross-buck sign with no distance range
choice_c: Within 5 feet of the nearest rail
choice_d: There is no minimum distance, only a maximum of 100 feet
explanation: A driver of a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the test, what might the examiner ask the applicant to report?
choice_a: The posted clearance or height
choice_b: The manufacturer of the overpass
choice_c: The exact GPS coordinates of the overpass
choice_d: The overpass is never discussed during the test
explanation: After driving under an overpass, the applicant may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was; after crossing a bridge, they may be asked the posted weight limit.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.9, Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: During the road test, is 'floating gears' (shifting without using the clutch) allowed?
choice_a: No, floating of gears is not allowed during the road test; the clutch must always be used to shift
choice_b: Yes, floating gears is the preferred method for CDL testing
choice_c: It is allowed only on downshifts
choice_d: Floating gears is required on unsynchronized transmissions
explanation: Applicants must always use the clutch to shift; floating of gears is not allowed during the road test. If equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, the driver must double-clutch when shifting.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.11(a), Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What happens if a driver coasts more than the length of the vehicle during the road test?
choice_a: It is an automatic failure
choice_b: It results in a minor point deduction only
choice_c: It is acceptable as long as it happens only once
choice_d: Coasting distance is not scored
explanation: Coasting more than the length of the vehicle is an automatic failure; drivers must not ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or 'pop' the clutch.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.11(a), Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: How should a driver apply the brakes during the road test, according to brake usage scoring criteria?
choice_a: Smoothly using steady pressure, without riding or pumping the brake
choice_b: By pumping the brakes rapidly for every stop
choice_c: By riding the brake lightly while accelerating
choice_d: Braking technique is not scored during the test
explanation: Brake usage scoring requires the driver not to ride or pump the brake, and not to brake harshly -- brakes should be applied smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.13(c), Brake Usage

question: In which lane should a driver finish a right turn on a multiple lane road during the road test?
choice_a: The right-most (curb) lane
choice_b: The center lane
choice_c: Any lane the driver prefers
choice_d: The lane directly to the left of the center line
explanation: Lane usage scoring requires the driver to finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane, and to finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.14(d), Lane Usage

question: According to the road test steering criteria, when should a driver's hands leave the steering wheel?
choice_a: Only while shifting, then both hands should return to the wheel
choice_b: Hands may leave the wheel at any time when driving straight
choice_c: One hand should remain off the wheel at all times for quick access to controls
choice_d: Hands should never leave the wheel, even to shift
explanation: Drivers must keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting; once the shift is completed, both hands should return to the steering wheel.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.15, Steering

question: If applying for a School Bus endorsement, what must the applicant demonstrate during the road test, and how far from students must the bus stop for discharge?
choice_a: A student discharge, bringing the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop
choice_b: A student discharge with no minimum stopping distance specified
choice_c: The school bus endorsement does not require any road test demonstration
choice_d: Students must be discharged while the bus is still moving slowly
explanation: An applicant for a School Bus endorsement must demonstrate a student discharge, bringing the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop, placing the transmission in neutral/park, setting the parking brake, and activating the stop arm and red warning lights.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version) -- Section 13.1.10, Student Discharge (School Bus)
